## With the speech recogniser loaded

VRAM alone hides what matters here: a card that is full keeps working, because the Windows driver pages what does not fit into shared system memory, and generation slows several-fold without an error. So the `v3-*` arms are read by speed as well.

| arm | phase | VRAM | turn p50 / p95 s | router first call p50 s | answer tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v3-8b` | Phase 3 | 9.0 GB | 3.8 / 7.3 | 2.3 | 130.3 |
| `v3-8b` | final | 9.6 GB | 4.2 / 6.9 | 2.5 | 120.0 |
| `v3-27b` | Phase 3 | 15.5 GB | 11.9 / 16.3 | 8.3 | 44.0 |
| `v3-27b` | final | 15.3 GB | 87.4 / 112.9 | 44.0 | 10.9 |
| `v3-27b` | final, context 6144 (rerun) | 15.2 GB | 61.7 / 75.3 | 28.5 | 13.7 |
| `v3-27b` | final, Ollama default context (rerun) | 15.3 GB | 97.6 / 124.2 | 32.2 | 10.6 |

The two context-size rows are the `v3-27b` arm run again back to back (runtime/evals/p3f-vram), the only difference being `ELAINA_NUM_CTX`.
